headline: Radio brings America the election
post_facts: KDKA aired the Harding vs Cox returns
Results came in by phone, live on air

scenes.text: [calmly] On this day, in nineteen twenty... a Pittsburgh radio station changed how America got its news.

scenes.label: KDKA microphone, 1920
scenes.caption: Later shown at the Smithsonian
scenes.text: [thoughtfully] Westinghouse station K-D-K-A read the presidential election returns live, as they came in by telephone.

scenes.label: Warren G. Harding
scenes.caption: Photo by Harris & Ewing
scenes.text: [calmly] Listeners heard Warren Harding beat James Cox in a landslide.

scenes.label: radio stations on the air by 1922
scenes.text: [thoughtfully] By nineteen twenty-two... about five hundred stations were on the air.

scenes.title: Do you still listen to the radio?
scenes.text: [gently] Do you still listen to the radio?
